text:
noah: Quick postmortem note from the midnight DR run. We had a tenant that observed successful reads from EU edge but writes were failing with residency errors while controller logs showed a successful swap to eu-central. Operators couldn't tell whether proxies were stale or controller took an action.

anya: can you paste the sequence of events? was this a controller-initiated swap or proxy disagreement?

noah: sequence: 1) consent service returned stale cache for acct-554 so controller re-evaluated placement and wrote /leases/acct-554 -> eu-central (evt-e9c). 2) proxies were still serving eu-west because their local lease cache hadn't been invalidated. 3) writes returned 403/residency-mismatch at eu-west; reads still ok.

cheng: do proxies not ack lease write currently? how do we track propagation?

noah: currently proxies log X-Region-Lease but there's no shared event id. Controller writes an event id in kv but we don't surface that to the proxies. So operator UI only saw region-unavailable alert without a linked lease-event.

devon: proposes: 1) add X-Lease-Event-Id header emitted to and from proxies on all edge responses; 2) controller atomically write event to kv with event_id and include reason (consent-cache-stale|manual|kv-fail); 3) operator timeline ingests lease events and correlates with proxy acks.

anya: +1. Also, add `X-Consent-Decision` header (allow|deny|defer) and `X-Consent-Source: cache|svc` so triage can see where the decision came from.

cheng: curious on semantics: if controller write fails (kv error), should controller still emit an event for visibility?

devon: yes — emit event with reason=kv-fail and set `critical=true` in event payload so operators can hunt. Proxies should ack best-effort. If ack missing after 15s trigger an alert.

noah: metric names suggestion: lease_event_published_total, lease_event_ack_latency_seconds, lease_event_missing_ack_count. Expose per-tenant labels for quick slicing.

anya: runbook change: when operator sees residency-mismatch + event with reason consent-cache-stale, first step is to query consent-service health and cache TTL. If consent-service degraded, escalate and mark event as "human-hold" until manual override.

cheng: what about active-active tenants that legitimately accept multi-region writes? We mustn't block those with fail-closed semantics. Controller should consult tenant.flags: if flags include multi_write, proceed. Otherwise apply fail-closed for residency-restricted.

devon: implementation plan: proxy change ~1 day to emit header if present; controller change to attach event_id to all lease writes + emit timeline event ~2 days; UI join + alerting ~1 week. Canary on a small set of tenants first.

sre-bot: [alert] new metric rule: lease_event_missing_ack_count > 0 for 1m will fire to oncall.

noah: action items: noah(controller owner) -> RFC + event schema; anya(proxy) -> header wire; cheng(ui) -> timeline join; devon(sre) -> metrics/alerts/runbook.

anya: one more: standardize header casing to kebab-case: X-Lease-Event-Id, X-Consent-Source, X-Consent-Decision. We'll document length limits (32 chars).

devon: +1. Also include a lightweight test harness in DR that injects delayed proxy ack to ensure alerts behave as expected.

noah: ok I'll draft RFC now and link here when ready. Follow-up sync tomorrow 10:00am PT. Thanks.
